stem: A jeepney leaves the terminal at 7:00 a.m. and travels at 40 km/h. At 8:00 a.m., a car leaves the same terminal on the same road at 60 km/h. At what time will the car catch up with the jeepney?
hints: By 8:00 a.m., the jeepney already has a head start. How far ahead is it?
Head start = 40 × 1 = 40 km. They go the same direction, so the car gains 60 − 40 = 20 km each hour.
Time to catch up = head start ÷ 20 km/h. Add that time to 8:00 a.m.

steps.action: Let t = the hours the car drives until it catches up.
The jeepney left 1 hour earlier, so it drives t + 1 hours.
When the car catches up, both have gone the same distance: 60 × t = 40 × (t + 1).
steps.why: Distance = rate × time for each vehicle.
40 × (t + 1) = 40t + 40. The 40 km is the jeepney's head start.
20 km/h is how much faster the car is. That is how fast it closes the gap.

steps.action: Divide both sides by 20: t = 40 ÷ 20 = 2 hours.
Check: by 10:00 a.m. the jeepney has gone 40 × 3 = 120 km and the car has gone 60 × 2 = 120 km. Same place. The car catches up at 10:00 a.m.

This divides the 40 km head start by 100 km/h, adding the speeds. They go the same direction, so the car closes the gap at 60 − 40 = 20 km/h.
This divides the 40 km head start by the car's speed, 60 km/h. But the jeepney keeps moving, so use the difference of the speeds.
This counts the 2 hours from 7:00 a.m. The 2 hours start when the car leaves at 8:00 a.m.
